_about: Reviewed investor identities. 'same': names verified to be one firm, shown under 'use'. 'different': look-alike names verified to be different firms; they are never merged. Each entry records the evidence and a source, so a reviewer can re-check it. Researched 10 November 2026.

same.evidence: Sympl's $6m seed (Dec 2021) was led by Dubai-based BECO Capital; the record credited it as 'Beco'.
The Kenya-focused VC that co-led Zanifu's $11.2m round; 'Beyond Capital' is its short form.
The Africa climate-tech VC that closed a $55m fund (TechCrunch, March 2025); Equator VC is the same firm.
same.source_headline: Equator closes $55M fund to bring more private capital to African climate tech (TechCrunch, 11 Mar 2025)

same.evidence: Enko Capital's fund bought Servair's Burger King business in Cote d'Ivoire (April 2026); the record credited it as 'Enko'.
Jonathan Oppenheimer's buyout of GZ Industries (Nov 2023) ran through Oppenheimer Partners Ltd.
Glint Fund II (May 2024) is announced by Glint Ventures; Wasla is in Glint's portfolio.
The Egyptian investor in both Lucky's Series B (2026) and Connect Money's seed (2024); its chairman Mohamed Farouk chairs Lucky's board.
One Nigerian early-stage fund written three ways in round announcements (Chowdeck, Klas, Mecho Autotech).
same.source_headline: Mecho Autotech gets $2.15M to expand vehicle maintenance and repair services in Nigeria (TechCrunch, 9 Feb 2022)

same.evidence: The East African private equity firm behind the Ascent Rift Valley funds; headlines call it 'PE firm Ascent Capital Africa' and 'fund investor Ascent'.
same.source_headline: PE Firm Ascent Capital Africa Seeks To Raise Ksh12B For Its Ascent Rift Valley Fund II (The Kenyan Wall Street, 6 Dec 2018)

same.evidence: The same African angel investor network, credited as 'E4E' in one round.
same.source_headline: Shiprazor raises $2.65m to build an intelligent logistics layer for African e-commerce (Africa Business Communities, 30 Apr 2026)

same.evidence: The Tigo Rwanda (2017) and Warid Uganda (2013) acquisitions were made by Airtel's African business.
same.source_headline: Airtel Snaps Up Tigo Rwanda (Connecting Africa, 19 Dec 2017)

different.evidence: Paystack's 2016 'Spark' is Jason Njoku's investment company; Spark Capital is a US venture firm (Andela).
Swoop's backer Variant is a US venture firm; Variant Investments co-led Kenya's Zanifu.
Flutterwave's round lists 'Endeavor', 54gene's lists 'Endeavor Capital'; no source links them.
A Nigerian investment fintech, TPG's Rise Fund and Rise Capital are three businesses.
An energy company and an African angel/venture investor.
Zimbabwe's Vision Group, a Saudi VC and a separate investment company.
